name: Is extra insulation required when turning a garage into living space?

mainEntity.name: Is extra insulation required when turning a garage into living space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, an uninsulated garage conversion will quickly become uncomfortable and drive up utility costs in central Florida. Garages typically have uninsulated exterior block walls, open ceiling joists, and concrete slabs that allow extreme heat gain and moisture infiltration. Proper remodeling involves building interior furring or stud walls to hold high-performance batt or rigid foam insulation, installing ceiling insulation with proper attic ventilation, and using a continuous vapor barrier on the slab. These steps keep indoor air comfortable, prevent mold development, and ensure compliance with Florida Energy Conservation codes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, adding wall and ceiling insulation along with vapor barriers is necessary to manage Florida heat, control humidity, and meet energy codes.
